meta.title: UnitedHealth: The Repair and the Referee
meta.dek: Hemsley has rebuilt the margin faster than he promised. In two days in November the government proposed to claw back part of the last decade's Medicare Advantage revenue, and the stock gave back the whole post-earnings rally and more. How much of that is a bill, and how much is fear?

meta.type: Managed care: insurer (UnitedHealthcare) plus care delivery, PBM and health data (Optum)
meta.stage: Turnaround (margin repair inside a mature franchise)

verdict.sentence: The repair is real and the CRUSH clawback is a bill worth about $7 a share probability-weighted, not the $62 the stock lost in two days; but even at [[price]] the probability-weighted case returns [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle, so non-holders still wait for [[entry]] and holders hold.
verdict.breaks_if: the medical cost ratio's fall turns out to be reserve releases and benefit cuts rather than durable underwriting, or extrapolated RADV audits survive in court and reach back to PY2018. Either one turns a margin recovery into a regulated utility margin.
verdict.next: 2027 outlook, by Dec 31; Fifth Circuit RADV ruling, pending
verdict.compounding: [[compounding]] (Base EPS growth is mostly margin repair)

call: UnitedHealth fell 15% in two sessions, from $412.02 on November 16 to [[price]] on November 18, after CMS proposed CRUSH, a rule that would extrapolate Medicare Advantage audit findings back to payment year 2018 with no fee-for-service adjuster. The bill is real but bounded. CMS puts recoveries at about $9 billion per payment year across the industry; at UnitedHealth's ~28% share that is ~$2.5 billion pre-tax a year, about $13 a share in present value if all nine back years are collected, and about $7 if, as I think, the rule has even odds in court [Estimate]. The market took $62 a share, about $56 billion. Cigna, which sold its Medicare Advantage book, fell 5% with it; most of the move is a sector de-rating on politics, not arithmetic. That does not make the stock cheap. I value the clawback as its own line ([[optionality_value]] of FY2031 value) and move five points from Bull to Bear for a Congress and an agency now pulling the same way. The probability-weighted value is [[pw_ev]], [[pw_return]] a year with the dividend, and spot implies about [[implied_bear]] Bear odds against my 30%. The market has gone from too hopeful to about right. The 2027 outlook, due before year-end, settles it: at $23 or above the Base holds; with an explicit RADV reserve, the Bear gains ground.

tests.claim: That the recovery is underwriting, not reserve releases.
tests.test: in the Q4/FY2026 release (**mid-January 2027**), the full-year medical cost ratio is at or below 88.1% and adjusted EPS is at least $20.50 ([Q3 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/731766/000073176626000255/earningsrelease3q26unh.htm)).
tests.if_fail: the Base normalized margin falls to ≈6.8% (Base $477; PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test1.verb]]** (entry [[test1.entry]]).

tests.claim: That 2027 starts the 13–16% path, CRUSH included.
tests.test: the 2027 outlook (promised **before year-end 2026**, at the latest in the Q4 release) guides FY2027 adjusted EPS to at least $23.00 with no RADV charge carved out of adjusted earnings ([Q3 call](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/13/unitedhealth-unh-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)).
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test2.verb]]** (entry [[test2.entry]]).

tests.claim: That extrapolated RADV stays contested and no remedy breaks the integrated model.
tests.test: the Fifth Circuit rules for Humana in *Humana v. Kennedy* (argued Oct 5, 2026) or the CRUSH final rule drops the PY2018 start; and through the FY2026 10-K (**February 2027**) no DOJ complaint or settlement seeks structural separation or more than $5B ([CMS fact sheet](https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/fact-sheets/comprehensive-regulations-uncover-suspicious-healthcare-crush-proposed-rule-cms-6098-p), [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/05/humana-medicare-advantage-radv-audits-lawsuit-hearing/)).
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Bull to Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test3.verb]]** (entry [[test3.entry]]); the CRUSH line is then valued at 80%, not 50%, which takes about $6 more off the PW EV.

return_math.price_implied: At 9%, spot needs FY2031 EPS of [[Priced-in.eps]] at 15×, about four-fifths of the way from my Bear to my Base. Perpetual cross-check: ≈$20B of unlevered owner earnings ex-float on a ≈$362B EV is a 5.5% yield, which at 9% prices ≈3.3% growth forever [Derived].
return_math.epv: $220–320 a share: five-year ex-float owner earnings of $17.8B ÷ 9% on an equity basis ($220), or the median 8.1% margin capitalized on an enterprise basis ($320). Spot is about 9% above the top of the range, so 9–37% of the price pays for growth. The Bear ([[Bear.value]]) sits inside it.
return_math.base_rate: The Bull's 6% nominal (~3.5% real) revenue growth sits between the 1.5% median and the ≥5%-real threshold (≈27% of >$50B companies) ([compounding.md](../../../frameworks/compounding.md)): Plausible. The Base's ~2% real is the median: Probable. The Bear is Probable now that CMS and Congress pull the same way.
return_math.terminal_growth: Implied perpetual growth at 9%: Bull [[Bull.g]], Base [[Base.g]], Bear [[Bear.g]], all below the ≈5.15% ten-year Treasury.
return_math.year_ten: Still growing at year ten: health spending and Medicare enrollment compound past 2036. The uncertainty is the regulated margin, not the runway.
return_math.rr_note: The Bear is a regulated utility margin, not a broken company; it earns ≈$20B of net income in 2031.
return_math.note: Computed rows come from model.json. Adjusted EPS excludes intangible amortization; SBC is ≈0.2% of revenue, so EPS and owner earnings converge.
